result.target_summary: Research and development expenses and sales, general, and administrative expenses increased in fiscal year 2024, primarily driven by compensation and benefits, including stock-based compensation, which reflected employee growth and compensation increases.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2024 disclosure explicitly combines R&D and SG&A expense increases driven by compensation. The 2023 previous disclosures D059 and D060 separately describe the increases in R&D expense and SG&A expense, respectively, both attributed to compensation and employee growth. These form the component parts of the 2024 consolidated discussion.

previous_disclosures.summary: Research and development expense for fiscal year 2023 increased primarily due to higher compensation, employee growth, engineering development costs, and data center infrastructure.
Sales, general and administrative expense for fiscal year 2023 increased primarily due to higher compensation and employee growth.

current_disclosures.summary: Research and development expenses and sales, general, and administrative expenses increased in fiscal year 2024, primarily driven by compensation and benefits, including stock-based compensation, which reflected employee growth and compensation increases.

materiality_analysis.reason: The change is primarily a structural reorganization of the disclosure, combining R&D and SG&A expenses into a single narrative rather than separate lines. The underlying drivers (compensation, employee growth) remain consistent and are not new risks or strategic shifts. The consolidation of the explanation does not materially change the substance of the expense increases.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Consolidation of R&D and SG&A expense narratives

previous_disclosures.summary: Research and development expenses and sales, general, and administrative expenses increased in fiscal year 2024, primarily driven by compensation and benefits, including stock-based compensation, which reflected employee growth and compensation increases.

current_disclosures.summary: Research and development expenses for fiscal year 2025 increased, driven by a 32% rise in compensation and benefits, a 100% increase in compute and infrastructure costs, and a 234% increase in engineering development costs for new product introductions.

materiality_analysis.reason: The explanation for R&D expense growth evolves from general 'compensation and benefits' in 2024 to specific, high-growth categories in 2025, including a 100% increase in compute/infrastructure costs and a 234% increase in engineering development costs. This highlights a strategic shift in R&D spending towards infrastructure and new product introductions, materially changing the nature of operating expense growth.

comparisons.peer_topic: R&D Expense Increase and AI Headcount
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's research and development expenses increased by 10% to $6.5 billion in 2024, primarily driven by higher employee-related costs resulting from an increase in headcount to support the company's AI strategy.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies attribute increases in Research and Development (R&D) expenses primarily to compensation and employee growth. NVDA states that the increase in R&D and SG&A was 'primarily driven by compensation and benefits, including stock-based compensation, reflecting employee growth and compensation increases,' while AMD notes its R&D expense increase was 'primarily due to higher employee-related costs due to an increase in headcount in support of our AI strategy.' Both disclosures highlight employee-related costs and headcount growth as the central drivers for rising R&D spend.

sentences.text: The increase in research and development expenses and sales, general and administrative expenses for fiscal year 2024 was primarily driven by compensation and benefits, including stock-based compensation, reflecting employee growth and compensation increases.
The increase was primarily due to higher employee-related costs due to an increase in headcount in support of our AI strategy.

comparisons.peer_summary: Marketing, general and administrative expenses were $2.8 billion in 2024, an increase of $431 million or 18% from $2.4 billion in 2023, primarily due to increased go-to-market activities supporting revenue growth.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose increases in Sales, General, and Administrative (SG&A) or Marketing, General, and Administrative (MG&A) expenses driven by commercial activities. NVDA identifies 'compensation and benefits' within its SG&A increase, whereas AMD specifically attributes its MG&A increase to 'go-to-market activities to support our revenue growth.' While the specific driver differs (headcount/compensation vs. strategic marketing activities), both represent the SG&A component of the broader operating expense discussion.

sentences.text: The increase in research and development expenses and sales, general and administrative expenses for fiscal year 2024 was primarily driven by compensation and benefits, including stock-based compensation, reflecting employee growth and compensation increases.
The increase was primarily due to an increase in go-to-market activities to support our revenue growth.
